cities.name: Moirang
cities.overview: A town on the edge of Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district, historically important as the headquarters of the Indian National Army in 1944.

cities.name: Imphal
cities.overview: Manipur's capital in an oval valley ringed by hills, known for its all-women Ima Market and its polo heritage.
cities.history: The seat of the Meitei kings at Kangla for centuries. It was a major Allied battleground against Japan in 1944, and it joined India in 1949.

cities.name: Ukhrul
cities.overview: A Tangkhul Naga hill town in the east of the state, known for the Shirui Lily.

places.name: Loktak Lake
places.shortDescription: The largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for its floating islands called phumdis.
places.description: Loktak Lake is covered with phumdis, floating mats of vegetation and soil, some large enough to hold fishermen's huts. The view from Sendra Island at sunset, with fishing boats weaving between the circular phumdis, is one of Manipur's classic sights. The lake supplies water, fish and hydroelectric power to much of the state. Check current travel advisories for Manipur before planning a visit.
places.history: Loktak was designated a Ramsar wetland of international importance in 1990. Its southern part forms Keibul Lamjao National Park.

places.name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
places.shortDescription: The world's only floating national park and the last natural home of the dancing sangai deer.
places.description: Keibul Lamjao covers about 40 km² of floating phumdis at the southern end of Loktak Lake. It is the only natural habitat of the sangai, the brow-antlered deer whose delicate gait on the floating marsh earned it the name 'dancing deer', and it is Manipur's state animal. Watchtowers on Babet hillock give the best chance of seeing them in the early morning. Hog deer, otters and many water birds also live here.
places.history: The park was created in 1977 after the sangai was thought extinct and then rediscovered in 1953. The Sangai Festival, held each November, is named after it.

places.name: Kangla Fort
places.shortDescription: The ancient seat of Manipur's kings, guarded by giant white dragon-lion statues in the heart of Imphal.
places.description: Kangla, on the banks of the Imphal River, was the political and religious centre of Manipur for centuries. Inside its moated grounds are the reconstructed Kangla Sha, two great white dragon-lion statues that are symbols of the state, along with ruined temples, sacred ponds and a museum. The open lawns are a pleasant place to walk. Nearby, the Ima Keithel market is run entirely by women.
places.history: Kangla was the seat of the Meitei kings until the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891, after which it was used by the British and later by the Assam Rifles. It was handed back to the state government in 2004 and opened to the public.

places.name: Ima Keithel
places.shortDescription: The Mothers' Market in Imphal, thought to be the largest women-run market in Asia.
places.description: Thousands of women sell fish, vegetables, textiles and crafts from raised stalls. It's a centre of Manipuri life and politics, and it has played a role in many protests.
places.history: Reported to date from the 16th century.
places.bestTimeNote: Manipur has had serious unrest in recent years, and visitors need an Inner Line Permit, so check current advice before planning a trip.

places.name: Shree Govindajee Temple
places.shortDescription: The largest Vaishnava temple in Imphal, next to the old royal palace, with twin gold domes.
places.description: A simple and beautiful temple with a large hall where Manipuri devotional dance is performed at festivals like Yaoshang.
places.bestTimeNote: Manipur has had serious unrest in recent years, and visitors need an Inner Line Permit, so check current advice before planning a trip.

places.name: Manipur State Museum
places.shortDescription: A museum in Imphal, with costumes, royal boats and arms from the Meitei kingdom.
places.description: A good introduction to Manipur's varied cultures, with a long royal boat and displays of tribal dress and crafts.
places.bestTimeNote: Manipur has had serious unrest in recent years, and visitors need an Inner Line Permit, so check current advice before planning a trip.

places.name: Shirui Kashong Peak
places.shortDescription: A hill near Ukhrul, the only home of the rare Shirui Lily, the state flower, which blooms in May.
places.description: A trek through grass and forest to the top of the peak, among the lilies that bloom nowhere else on earth. A festival is held in May.
places.bestTimeNote: Manipur has had serious unrest in recent years, and visitors need an Inner Line Permit, so check current advice before planning a trip.
